_readme: One file every language reads: the agent harnesses OpenBot knows by name. The desktop setup window reads it through Rust (desktop/src-tauri/src/harness.rs, include_str!) to decide which image to run; the web app's New Bot dialog reads it through shared/harnesses.ts to name the frameworks a person might already be running. Ranked stars-first, with downloads as the sanity check, because each misleads alone. Anything the AG-UI table marks In Progress is left out — OpenAI's Agents SDK, AWS Bedrock Agents and Cloudflare Agents are all In Progress, and offering a harness that cannot answer is worse than a shorter list. 'image' is the DIRECTORY the image is built from, not the id: a release publishes openbot-<directory> from the Dockerfile paths in the tree, and four rows have an id that differs from their folder. 'mark' is the file stem under shared/marks/, or null where no maintained set has one — nothing is ever invented to fill the gap, see shared/marks/README.md. 'desktopCreate' is false for a row the desktop create flow must not offer; the picker then disables it and Tauri refuses a direct or stale choice of it, and 'desktopUnavailableReason' gives the person the reason. It is null exactly when 'desktopCreate' is true. 'webCreate' is false for a row the web create API cannot actually make work; a row can be closed on one surface and open on the other, so each flag is set on its own. A gated row stays in this file, with its adapter and image directory, so the package is tracked while creation is closed. Re-enabling Codex takes the evidence listed under 'Keep Codex unavailable for creation' in docs/architecture/decisions.md, not a flag change alone. 'webSummary' overrides 'summary' in the web dialog, and exists only where the installer's sentence is false on a surface that installs nothing.
